title: Hide desktop and apps behind a smoothly-animating "shutdown screen" while shutting down, unless a window wants attention; then raise it above the screen so it can take input
line: When you log out, the screen now fades to black while apps close, and only "Save changes?" prompts and the logout notification stay visible on top.
explanation: After you confirmed logging out, the desktop, panel and apps stayed on screen for several seconds as if nothing had happened, and "Save changes?" prompts showed up over the full desktop. KWin's internal Session Quit effect was supposed to react to the quitting state, but KWin's setState() D-Bus method read ksmserver's values shifted by one (saving became quitting, quitting became normal, and normal after a cancel became saving), so KWin never was in the right state at the right time. Also, cancelling a Wayland logout never told KWin the session was back to normal. KWin now maps the states as its D-Bus interface documents, and the Session Quit effect fades every window to black (600 ms, follows the animation speed) once the session quits; modal dialogs and windows that appear while quitting (the apps' prompts, the "applications did not close" notification with Cancel Logout) stay visible above the black and take input. ksmserver's resetLogout() now sets KWin back to normal, so cancelling fades the desktop back in.

commits.message:
plugins/sessionquit: Fade windows to black while logging out

Logging out kept the desktop on screen for seconds, and setState() read
ksmserver's states shifted by one. Map them as documented and fade all
windows to black while quitting, except modal dialogs and new prompts.

BUG: 188476

ksmserver: Return KWin to the normal state when logout is cancelled

When an application kept a Wayland logout from finishing and the user
cancelled it, KWin stayed in the quitting state and kept the screen
black. Tell KWin that the session is back to normal in resetLogout().

BUG: 188476

patches.diff:
From 40893ff5204ec1f188170e0b682ee06e410310e4 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 13:25:01 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] ksmserver: Return KWin to the normal state when logout is
 cancelled

When an application kept a Wayland logout from finishing and the user
cancelled it, KWin stayed in the quitting state and kept the screen
black. Tell KWin that the session is back to normal in resetLogout().

BUG: 188476
---
 ksmserver/logout.cpp | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

diff --git a/ksmserver/logout.cpp b/ksmserver/logout.cpp
index c1daa435d7..c21b482401 100644
--- a/ksmserver/logout.cpp
+++ b/ksmserver/logout.cpp
@@ -431,4 +431,5 @@ void KSMServer::timeoutQuit()
 void KSMServer::resetLogout()
 {
     state = Idle;
+    m_kwinInterface->setState(KWinSessionState::Normal);
 }
--

media.caption: Master: logging out with Dolphin and an app with unsaved changes. The desktop stays up for seconds, then the prompt appears over the full desktop.
Fixed: the screen fades to black, the prompt and the notification stay on top; Cancel Logout fades the desktop back in, and logging out again fades it out again.
Master, 3 s after confirming: the full desktop is still there.
Fixed, same moment: everything is black except the app's "Save changes?" prompt.
Master: prompt and "did not close" notification over the desktop.
Fixed: prompt and notification over black, both usable.
